Vue's v-bind and v-model for a component's arguments

Source: R/vue_directives.R
v_bind.Rd

A component's argument given v_bind() or v_model() in place of a value follows state on the page, in the browser, with no round trip to the server – as :size="size" and v-model="open" do in a Vue template. The page's UI state stays in the browser; the server keeps the data and the decisions.

Usage

v_bind(expr, ns = NULL)

v_model(path, ns = NULL)

Arguments

expr

A JavaScript expression over $vueStore, $inputs and $route, a string.

ns

In a module, its namespace: the function shiny::NS() gives, session$ns, or the module's id.

path

A store's field, $vueStore.<id>.<field>, going on with .<name>, ['<name>'] or [<index>].

Value

The binding, to give as an argument's value.

Details

  • v_bind(expr) is one way, as v-bind (:prop="expr"): the argument follows the expression, any JavaScript expression – v_bind("$inputs.fold === 'collapse'").

  • v_model(path) is both ways, as v-model: the argument follows a store's field, and when the component's user changes it – a dialog closed, a value picked – the field is set, so everything bound to it follows. The path is one a value can be assigned to: v_model("$vueStore.ui.open").

Each component is a Vue application of its own, so an expression sees the page, not another component's variables: the names it can use are

  • $vueStore.<id>: a vue_store(), its state and getters;

  • $inputs.<id>: the value a component reports as input$<id>, as its component reports it (before any debounce, before an input handler converts it);

  • $route: the route of the page's vue_router() – $route.path, $route.params.id.

Given a bound argument, update_*() sets the field; with v_model() that sets the store too, so everything bound to it follows; with v_bind() the field keeps the update until the expression changes. v_bind() on a component's value makes it controlled: it starts from and follows the expression, and its user's change stays the component's until the expression changes. With Shiny on the page the component reports input$<id> as ever, so the server sees what the page did.

What can be bound: any of a component's props and its value, and what a dialog's, drawer's, tabs' or collapse's update_*() can set. An argument R reads to draw the component – a label, the choices, a class – says it cannot be bound.

Modules

Give ns, the module's shiny::NS() or its id, and the expression is left as written while its names are the module's: $inputs.size is input$size of the module, $vueStore.ui the store made with vue_store(ns("ui")) – as input$size is inside shiny::moduleServer(). Without ns, the names are the page's, and a store named the same in two instances of a module is one store.

See also

v_on() for acting in the browser; vue_store() for state shared by components.

Examples

# A size picked in one component, followed by another
htmltools::tagList(
  vue_app(
    "size",
    htmltools::tags$select(
      `v-model` = "size",
      htmltools::tags$option("small"),
      htmltools::tags$option("large")
    ),
    data = list(size = "small"),
    input = "size"
  ),
  vue_app(
    "shown",
    htmltools::tags$span("Large: {{ large }}"),
    data = list(large = v_bind("$inputs.size === 'large'"))
  )
)
#> <div id="size" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><select v-model="size">
#>   <option>small</option>
#>   <option>large</option>
#> </select></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"size":"small"}},"input":"size","evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="shown" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span>Large: {{ large }}</span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"large":null}},"bound":{"large":{"expr":"$inputs.size === 'large'"}},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>

# A store, set by one and followed by another
htmltools::tagList(
  vue_store("ui", state = list(open = FALSE)),
  vue_app(
    "toggle",
    htmltools::tags$button(`@click` = "open = !open", "Toggle"),
    data = list(open = v_model("$vueStore.ui.open"))
  ),
  vue_app("state", htmltools::tags$span("{{ $vueStore.ui.open }}"))
)
#> <div id="ui" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span hidden></span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"open":false}},"store":true,"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="toggle" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><button @click="open = !open">Toggle</button></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":{"open":null}},"bound":{"open":{"expr":"$vueStore.ui.open","model":true}},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>
#> <div id="state" data-shiny-vue style="display: contents">
#>   <script type="text/x-template" data-shiny-vue-template><span>{{ $vueStore.ui.open }}</span></script>
#>   <script type="application/json" data-shiny-vue-options>{"options":{"data":[]},"evals":[]}</script>
#> </div>

# In a module: the module's input and store
panel_ui <- function(id) {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)
  htmltools::tagList(
    vue_store(ns("ui"), state = list(open = FALSE)),
    vue_app(
      ns("shown"),
      htmltools::tags$span("{{ open }}"),
      data = list(open = v_bind("$vueStore.ui.open", ns = ns))
    )
  )
}
